titles.Root of penis & perineum: Root of the penis and perineum

clinical: Digital rectal exam
Digital rectal examination palpates the prostate through the front wall of the rectum. A hard, irregular nodule felt there raises suspicion of prostate cancer.
Fluid in the rectovesical pouch
The rectovesical pouch is the lowest part of the male peritoneal cavity, so blood, pus or tumour deposits from the abdomen collect there and can be felt on rectal examination.
Painless testicular lump
Most testicular tumours are germ cell tumours that start in the seminiferous tubules. A painless, firm lump in the testis needs prompt medical assessment.
Epididymitis
Inflammation of the epididymis causes pain and swelling at the back of the testis. In sexually active young men it is most often caused by chlamydia or gonorrhoea.
Hydrocele

A hydrocele is fluid collecting in the tunica vaginalis, the serous sac around the front of the testis. It causes painless scrotal swelling that transilluminates, meaning a light shone behind it glows through.
Cremasteric reflex
Stroking the inner thigh makes the cremaster muscle contract and lift the testis. This reflex tests the L1-L2 nerve supply.
Indirect inguinal hernia
An indirect inguinal hernia passes through the deep inguinal ring, lateral to the inferior epigastric artery, and then along the inguinal canal inside the spermatic cord into the scrotum.
Testicular torsion

Twisting of the spermatic cord cuts off blood flow to the testis, causing sudden severe pain. It is a surgical emergency, because the testis is often lost if the cord is not untwisted within about 6 hours.
Urethral tear in pelvic fracture

The membranous urethra is held fixed by the puboprostatic ligaments, so it is the part most often torn in pelvic fractures. Blood at the urethral opening after a pelvic injury suggests this kind of tear.
Reflux from the bladder

The ureter enters the bladder obliquely, and this arrangement works as a flap valve that stops urine flowing back up. If the valve fails, urine refluxes up the ureter, raising the risk of kidney infection.
Benign prostatic enlargement
The transition zone enlarges with age and squeezes the prostatic urethra. This causes difficulty starting to pass urine, a weak stream and frequent urination.
Prostate cancer
About 70% of prostate cancers arise in the peripheral zone, which lies at the back of the gland and is felt on rectal examination.
Penile fracture
Rupture of the tunica albuginea during forceful bending of an erect penis causes a penile fracture. It is a urological emergency that usually needs surgical repair.
Erectile dysfunction

Erection depends on arterial blood filling the corpora cavernosa and on the tunica albuginea trapping that blood. Narrowed arteries, for example from atherosclerosis, are a common cause of erectile dysfunction.
Straddle injury
A blow to the perineum, such as a fall onto a bar, can crush the bulb of the penis against the pubic arch and tear the spongy urethra.
Bulbocavernosus reflex

Squeezing the glans or tugging a urinary catheter makes the bulbospongiosus contract. Testing this reflex checks the S2-S4 spinal segments, and loss of it suggests damage to the sacral cord or its nerves.
Klinefelter syndrome
In Klinefelter syndrome (47,XXY) the seminiferous tubules are small and hyalinised, so sperm production fails and the testes stay small and firm.
Undescended testis
Spermatogenesis needs a temperature a few degrees below core body temperature, so a testis that fails to descend into the scrotum has impaired sperm production and a higher risk of germ cell tumour.
Kartagener syndrome

Absent dynein arms in the axoneme cause primary ciliary dyskinesia, which is called Kartagener syndrome when situs inversus is also present. The sperm tails are immotile, so affected men are usually infertile, and airway cilia fail, causing chronic chest and sinus infections.
Intracytoplasmic sperm injection
In intracytoplasmic sperm injection a single sperm is injected straight into an egg, bypassing the acrosome reaction and zona pellucida. It is used for severe male infertility.
